note: Precedent registry. Approved precedents are the approved rules listed in the framework deck (slide 12). Each was assigned a fictional insurer from a separate name set (none of the 10 submitting insurers) and an illustrative approval year. These assignments are invented for the prototype and are flagged illustrative. Framework common examples come from slide 3. Illustrative non-compliant examples come from slide 5.

precedents.ruleText: 1 or more Criminal Code convictions in the preceding 3 years
2 or more at-fault accidents in the preceding 3 years
2 minor convictions within the preceding 3 years and 2 cancellations for non-payment of premium within the preceding 3 years
1 at-fault accident in the preceding 5 years and 1 minor conviction within the preceding 3 years and 2 cancellations for non-payment of premium within the preceding 3 years
1 or more convictions for auto insurance fraud in the preceding 10 years
Any automobile used for commercial purposes
Used on a racetrack, or in any race, speed test, or competition
Vehicles used for the purpose for which they were not designed
If no driver of the vehicle insured under the contract holds a valid Canadian licence to drive
Vehicles used for police work
Failure to pay any outstanding premiums owed to the insurer or its affiliated companies for the same named insured
Improper class of license or invalid license
Any vehicle modified for speed or used for racing
Any vehicle with unacceptable customizations or modifications
Use of personal vehicle for business purposes (consumer needs commercial insurance)
Part-time use of vehicle for package delivery
Deny insurance on any rebuilt vehicles
A pattern of at-fault accidents and tickets over a 3-year period
A combination of at-fault accidents or tickets over a short period AND cancellations for missed payments
A previous fraud conviction
Deny insurance on the basis that someone has never had insurance before
precedents.reason: Fails basic compliance: penalises consumers for having no insurance history, which blocks new drivers from mandatory coverage.

precedents.ruleText: Deny insurance to anyone with a vehicle that is one of the top three most stolen vehicles in Ontario
precedents.reason: Not aligned with the principles and fair consumer outcomes: penalises owners of popular vehicles for theft risk better handled through rating or anti-theft requirements.

precedents.ruleText: Deny insurance to people who drive red cars on the basis that they are likely to drive faster
precedents.reason: Subjective and arbitrary: no direct relationship with the risk.

precedents.ruleText: Deny insurance to someone accused of a crime they were not convicted of
precedents.reason: Relies on an accusation, not a conviction.

precedents.ruleText: Deny insurance to someone who changed insurers more than two times in 10 years
precedents.reason: Arbitrary and not directly related to driving risk; switching insurers is normal consumer behaviour.
